adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.challenge: Is this a blanket find-and-replace wearing a classification?
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.answer: No, and the diff proves it. The ten line28 sites split 7 to line14 and 2 to line06, with 1 kept. The five line14 sites all went to line06. Three destinations from two sources. A blanket replace could not produce that shape.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.challenge: Did I find zero legitimate line28 uses, which the dispatch flags as suspicious?
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.answer: No. One survives inside SettingsModal (the 2px Aside marker) and four more render ON the Settings surface from shared kit and were deliberately not touched: Button.tsx:50 primary, the quiet OUTLINE BUTTON named verbatim in the token doc; StatusChip.tsx:42 and :56 dashed absence chips; pe-tokens.css:283 .pe-btn:hover border. Every one is a control state or a signal, which is what the token means.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.challenge: The Aside call is close. What if it is wrong?
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.answer: Stated as close in CP1 with the counter-reading. It is one token at one call site (SettingsModal.tsx:102) and V2 proves the pins would catch its removal, so a reversal is a one-line change plus one expectation.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.challenge: Am I claiming a visual result?
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.answer: No. There is no screenshot harness in this repo. Nothing here asserts how the panel looks. The measured contrast numbers are arithmetic on hex values, not a rendering.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.challenge: Does the change do anything, or is it a correct artifact that enforces nothing?
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnChange.answer: The change is the rendered border colour on eleven structural elements, so it acts by definition. The PIN is the part at risk of being ceremonial, and V1 through V5 are the evidence it is not: it was observed FAILING five times, including once on a mutation that keeps every count identical.

Named honestly. (a) A line painted in a CSS file rather than an inline style; the sweep shows Settings has none today, but the pin would not see one added. (b) A NEW file added to the Settings tree; SETTINGS_TREE is a hand-listed array of three files, which is a hand-declared list and drifts the way every hand-declared list in this operation drifts. (c) A swap between two edges or between two rules that are not one of the three site-pinned lines. These are the exclusion set, and they are part of the instrument's contract.
